verdict.rationale: Stripe documents virtual cards scoped to a single task or session that are automatically invalidated after use, which covers the single-use core. Spending controls add per-authorization limits and merchant-ID blocking, but the evidence shows only blocking lists and caps, not locking a card to one merchant or an exact amount. Real-time authorization webhooks could enforce tighter rules, but that is a build-it-yourself primitive. Missing for 10: documented single-merchant allow-locking, exact-amount matching (rather than a per-authorization cap), single-use documentation outside the agents context, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can issue single-use and tightly scoped cards — one purchase, one merchant, an exact amount — so a leaked number is worthless the moment it's used

citations.quote: Issue virtual cards scoped to a single task or session. Cards are automatically invalidated after use.
You can use spending controls to block merchant categories (for example, bakeries), countries, merchant IDs, or card presence, and to set spending limits per authorization or per month.
